title: fix(tasks): avoid unknown status for live CLI tasks
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes active CLI-backed tasks showing “Activity unknown” when their live run is known but transient activity events have not arrived or were cleared.

## User Impact

Task details show Running or Queued from the exact live run and update automatically as ownership or queue capacity changes. Explicit waits and unavailable-runtime observations remain authoritative. No configuration, schema, or migration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Task status previously depended on the transient activity cache even though the run registry already held current execution ownership. The task reader now uses that existing owner when activity is absent, checks the resolved session and agent identity, and republishes task summaries through the existing deduplicated notification path. Capacity and queue-lease changes publish through the run registry, including for runs that suppress session lifecycle updates.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the missing read-time status and missing push updates before their fixes, including lifecycle-suppressed runs, queue leases, and stored tasks without an explicit agent ID.
- 151 focused tests passed across task Gateway handlers, task observations, runtime subscriptions and shutdown, agent events, and queue liveness.
- Changed-file checks passed, including production/test typechecks, lint, formatting, import-cycle checks, and repository guards.
- Independent review findings were fixed. A final duplicate-publication warning was rejected because the existing summary deduplication returns before broadcast; the no-duplicate regression passes.
- Backend status correction only; no Control UI rendering or appearance changes. Live deployment was not performed.

<details>
<summary>After-change proof through a real isolated Gateway</summary>

At rebased PR head `d85e2be82432`, an isolated loopback Gateway with synthetic state and a paired, signed WebSocket client exercised `tasks.get` and the actual task notification stream. A synthetic CLI run was registered without emitting agent activity. No model request or production deployment was involved.

```text
before live owner: tasks.get -> unknown
live owner, no activity events: tasks.get -> running
waiting for capacity: tasks.get -> queued
capacity available: tasks.get -> running
owner released: tasks.get -> unknown
WebSocket task updates: unknown -> running -> queued -> running -> unknown
```

Every state and the complete pushed sequence were asserted; the Gateway shut down cleanly.

</details>

CI note: the first run hit an intermittent workspace-lock timeout in an unchanged memory-core test. The unchanged focused test passed locally, and a Linux diagnostic run passed all 70 memory index tests in their original order with successful lease cleanup ([diagnostic run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35413364547)). No speculative memory change is included; the exact failed CI job passed on its single diagnostic rerun at the unchanged PR head ([successful job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35411400730/job/105816961969)).

Rebase verification: preserved the background-command status owner introduced by #152333 alongside this agent-run fix. The only manual conflict was the import list; the PR delta is unchanged apart from main context. After rebasing, 80 focused tests passed across the two task execution owners, Gateway task handling and subscriptions, and background command tracking. The isolated Gateway/WebSocket trace above was replayed successfully on the rebased head. Fresh required CI passed for that exact head ([CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35416698886/job/105828758927)).
